audit.report: A batch job (batch_replayable_price_sync, pid 338444) held a lock idle-in-transaction for over 4 seconds, blocking checkout sessions and degrading success to 28% over 30 seconds against a 95% SLO. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker, but a memory veto (MEM-1) recorded that a prior termination of this same workload failed to recover checkout (26% success). The Continuity Guardian accepted escalation because waiting would cost ~$132k in lost revenue and exceed the 60-second degradation tolerance, yet termination was historically ineffective. Both guardians agreed the decision required human judgment and escalated to the pricing team. No automated action was executed; the incident remained open after 30 seconds.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_price_sync job held a lock idle-in-transaction, blocking checkout sessions and causing sustained SLO violation.
lessons: For batch_replayable_price_sync: add a pre-flight check that the job is not idle-in-transaction before it acquires long-held locks, or enforce a strict statement_timeout to prevent idle hold.

For batch_replayable_price_sync: create a verified runbook for safe termination (e.g., cancel via scheduler, confirm replay starts) since direct process kill has a documented memory veto (MEM-1) of ineffectiveness.
For batch_replayable_price_sync: define a change-calendar window or maintenance policy that explicitly permits interruption, so the Continuity Guardian can approve termination without escalation.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian correctly honored the memory veto and did not waste a round re-proposing termination; the Continuity Guardian accepted escalation on the first round after reviewing the trade-off, so no guardian missed evidence or was overridden by an invariant.
follow_ups: Pricing team to confirm whether batch_replayable_price_sync can be safely cancelled via its scheduler (Airflow/Control-M) and replayed within the 2-minute replay SLA.
Engineering to instrument batch_replayable_price_sync with a statement_timeout and/or idle-in-transaction watchdog to prevent lock-holding stalls.
Platform to register a change-calendar exception for batch_replayable_price_sync so future incidents can be auto-remediated without human escalation.
